# Working a red gate or a slow Stop hook

A failing gate is a claim about the tree. Find out WHOSE claim before fixing anything.

## 1. Measure before you diagnose
- `.harness/log/dispatch.jsonl` -> `duration_ms` per event: pre-done, pre-commit, post-edit.
- The lane's `.harness/log/stages.jsonl` -> which gates recorded, and `partial`. Read
  `partial` first: since harness 33ce3f5 (G-11) a killed sweep names the gate it cut off,
  how long it had run and its position (`... while cargo-tests was running (Ns in, gate 4
  of 6 ...)`, and `partial.running` in the bundle). A row from an older pin records only
  the gates that FINISHED, so there the expensive one is the first bound gate missing.
- The lane's `.harness/log/lock.jsonl` -> `waited_ms`. Zero waits means contention is not
  the story, whatever the hook message says.
Never call it a hang without these three. 2026-09-27: 10 of 51 pre-done runs were at the
295s ceiling and six sweeps were killed at 1200s, and none of it was lock contention.

## 2. A red gate is not automatically yours
`git log -3 -- <the failing input>` and `git log -3 -- <the reading or pin it is compared
against>`. If the input moved after the reading was last regenerated, the red belongs to
the commit that moved it. The style gate failed because CF-11 and CF-12 regenerated the
subset skills after JV-3 last re-ran the reading.

## 3. Attribute a reading failure by INPUT SET before calling it a regression
Only forge-authored sets fail (skill-examples, new-templates, oracle-fixtures); census-ops
is a reading. "29 rules over baseline" was 30 rows of NEW oracle fixtures and zero
movement in the taught text. Diff the sets, don't read the total.

## 4. Growth is accepted by name, never ratcheted quietly
`style-gate.py ratchet --accept-growth "<why>"` refuses any grown rule with no owner, and
that refusal is the check on you. Name the step that added the files. `ratchet` alone only
lowers; that is what makes it a bar.

## 5. A test that reads a sibling checkout may be failing on staleness
`git fetch` and compare local to origin BEFORE concluding code is missing. `branch
--contains <sha>` lies when the local ref is stale: forge-runtime's main checkout was six
commits behind, which read as "CF-11's fix is stranded on a lane branch" when it was on
origin/main all along. Sweep the fleet with a behind/ahead/dirty loop when in doubt.

## 6. A verifier that did not execute has not passed
Read the bundle, not the summary: `executed`, `skip_reason`, `result`. Since 33ce3f5 (G-10,
D-119) a skip writes no `intent-aligned` event, and every event says its `basis`. So when
align -> review refuses, there are two routes, in this order:
- The diff is real but the judge did not see it (work already committed, e.g. by per-turn
  checkpoints): `runner.py pre-review --diff-base <merge-base>`. The driver passes this
  itself now; do it by hand only outside a driven run. Record the bundle id in evidence.
- No intent judge's path_filters cover the diff (bookkeeping, docs, scripts):
  `dispatch.py intent align --reason '<why no judge sees this diff>'`. It is recorded as
  `basis: operator`, visibly not a verdict, and refused while any judge covers the diff —
  if it refuses, the judge is the route.

## 7. Never escape a gate that cannot finish
`FORGE_HARNESS_UNGOVERNED` past a ceiling is how CF-11 landed with its suites run by hand
and its gate never run. A gate that cannot finish inside its own ceiling is a defect in the
machine: file it with the measurement. Same for a requirement no lane can satisfy.

## 8. Changing an instrument means resealing and re-reading it
A census or style input that matches no gate's include glob lands ungated, and the gate will
later name YOUR commit as its owner. `refusal-census.py gate --ratchet --reseal` after any
corpus, control or schema.lock change. If you cannot re-read it, say so in the commit
message rather than implying you did.

## 9. Say what you could not verify, and correct it when you learn
Two claims today needed retracting: "the fix is stranded on a lane branch" (it was on
origin/main) and "29 regressions in the taught examples" (they were new fixtures). Both were
caught by running one more command. Prefer the command to the inference, and correct plainly.

## 10. Where you work decides what a Stop costs
forge-sdlc-harness's sweep is Python tests and returns in seconds. forge-lang's is 1605
tests and 20+ minutes. Do harness work in the harness repo. Since 33ce3f5 (G-11, D-120):
an EMPTY change set at pre-done tests nothing (paths from `wip:` checkpoints since the last
step commit still count), and the Stop sweep runs under one 1200 s budget in which a gate
whose recorded cost cannot fit is deferred to the post-commit verify, with the reason in
evidence. A deferral is not a pass: the step commit still owes the suite. A watcher moves
the wait off the hook; it does not shorten it — one forge-lang pass took 22 minutes, held
the build lock and was superseded before anything adopted it. Start one only where the
suite fits inside an edit cycle.

## 11. Two mechanics of this box
- There is no `timeout(1)`. Use the python subprocess form the hook prints.
- Background a long run and wait on ITS log. A launcher's exit is not the job's exit; a
  notification on the launcher means nothing finished.

## 12. What a filed gap must carry
Measured cost in numbers, the fixtures that reproduce it (real bundle or evidence paths), an
acceptance item that only a fix can satisfy, and a "measured after" item in the same units.
G-10 and G-11 are the shape.
